accepted.s: Under Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, a minority is defined as:
o: A community notified as such by the Central Government
A linguistic group notified by the Special Officer under Article 350B
A community having less than 10 per cent of the national population
A community recognised by the Supreme Court
accepted.x: Section 2(c) of the NCM Act, 1992, treats a minority as any community notified as such by the Central Government. The Act itself does not define the term in general constitutional terms.
accepted.tq: Use the exact statutory definition and distinguish it from constitutional references.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s:
Which of the following communities were notified as minorities in 1993 under the National Commission for Minorities framework?
1. Muslims
2. Christians
3. Sikhs
4. Buddhists
5. Parsis
6. Jains
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists and Parsis were notified in 1993. Jains were added later, on 27 January 2014.
accepted.tq: Separate the original notified group from the community added later.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s: Jains were notified as a minority community by the Central Government on:
accepted.x: Jains were notified as a minority community on 27 January 2014. Before this notification, 11 States had already declared Jains as a minority.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely associated notification years and dates.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before the Central notification of 2014, 11 States had already declared Jains a minority.
2. The six notified minority communities together constitute more than 19 per cent of India’s population.
3. The Ministry of Minority Affairs was established in 1992.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Ministry of Minority Affairs was set up in 2006, not in 1992.
accepted.tq: Check the dates carefully while retaining the supported population figure.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was set up in 2006. Haj management was added to its work from:
accepted.x: The Ministry of Minority Affairs was established in 2006, and Haj management was added to its responsibilities from October 2016.
accepted.tq: Match an institutional milestone with the precise year and month given.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s: In the T.M.A. Pai case, the 11-judge Bench held that religious and linguistic minorities should be identified:
o: By the National Commission for Minorities alone
accepted.x: The T.M.A. Pai 11-judge Bench held that religious and linguistic minorities are to be identified at the State level. States may therefore notify their own minorities.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct constitutional level instead of assuming a national classification.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of linguistic minorities?
o: They are dealt with only by the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
They are notified under Section 2(c) of the NCM Act.
They are excluded from constitutional protection.
They fall under the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B.
accepted.x: Linguistic minorities are not notified under the NCM Act. They come under the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities mentioned in Article 350B.
accepted.tq: Distinguish religious minorities under the NCM Act from linguistic minorities under Article 350B.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments relating to the National Commission for Minorities in chronological order:
A. Non-statutory Minorities Commission constituted by a Ministry of Home Affairs resolution
B. NCM Act made the Commission statutory and the body renamed NCM
C. First statutory Commission constituted
D. Vice-Chairperson added and the strength became seven
Select the correct sequence.
accepted.x: The correct sequence is 1978, 1992, 1993 and 1995: the non-statutory Commission, the NCM Act, the first statutory Commission and the addition of the Vice-Chairperson.
accepted.tq: Use the milestone years to establish the sequence from origin to statutory expansion.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
 a. 1978
 b. 1992
 c. 1993
 d. 1995

List-II
 i. First statutory Commission constituted
 ii. Vice-Chairperson added
 iii. Non-statutory Minorities Commission formed
 iv. NCM Act made the body statutory

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: The milestones are correctly matched as 1978–non-statutory Commission, 1992–statutory NCM Act, 1993–first statutory Commission and 1995–addition of Vice-Chairperson.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure year-event pair and eliminate codes with mismatched milestones.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s:
With reference to the composition of the National Commission for Minorities, consider the following statements:
1. It consists of a Chairperson, a Vice-Chairperson and five Members.
2. All seven members must belong to minority communities.
3. Five of the seven members, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities.
4. The term of office is three years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Commission has seven members: a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and five Members. Five, including the Chairperson, must be from minority communities, and the term is three years; it is not required that all seven belong to minority communities.
accepted.tq: Test composition, qualification and tenure separately to catch the overstatement in ‘all’.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s: The members of the National Commission for Minorities are nominated by the:
accepted.x: The Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and five Members of the Commission are nominated by the Central Government. They are not nominated by the President.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ test to identify the appointing authority.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s: The Constitution refers to the term ‘minority’ in which of the following Articles, without defining it?
accepted.x: The Constitution uses the term ‘minority’ in Articles 29, 30, 350A and 350B, but does not provide a general definition of the term.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact Article group rather than selecting a familiar Fundamental Rights cluster.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function or power associated with the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Issuing binding judicial decrees in all matters concerning minorities
Looking into complaints relating to minority safeguards
accepted.x: The Commission evaluates minority development, monitors safeguards and looks into complaints. Its recommendations are advisory; it does not issue binding judicial decrees.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that converts an advisory statutory body into a court.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s: While inquiring into matters, the National Commission for Minorities has powers similar to those of a civil court for purposes such as:
o: Summoning witnesses and calling for records
accepted.x: The Commission has civil-court powers while inquiring, including summoning witnesses and calling for records. Its recommendations remain advisory.
accepted.tq: Separate procedural civil-court powers from substantive judicial and legislative powers.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s: The National Commission for Minorities works under the:
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
accepted.x: The National Commission for Minorities works under the Ministry of Minority Affairs. The earlier non-statutory Commission had been formed through a Ministry of Home Affairs resolution.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ministry associated with the present statutory body from its earlier origin.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding institutions related to minority affairs?
1. The National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions was established under an Act of 2004.
2. Statutory State Minority Commissions exist in 19 States/Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Both statements are correct. The National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions is associated with the 2004 Act, and statutory State Minority Commissions exist in 19 States/Union Territories including Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Combine two independently verifiable institutional facts and test the ‘both’ option.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the National Commission for Minorities is correct?
o: The Chairperson is appointed for a one-year term only.
The Commission has no Chairperson and is headed by the Special Officer under Article 350B.
The Delhi High Court permanently abolished the Commission because of vacancies.
Harjit Singh Grewal was appointed Chairperson for a full three-year term.
accepted.x: Harjit Singh Grewal was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities for a full three-year term. A separate matter concerned the Delhi High Court seeking the Centre’s response on long-pending vacancies.
accepted.tq: Separate a current appointment fact from a related judicial development.
accepted.sec: Notified minorities under the NCM Act - communities and year of notification

accepted.s: According to the 2011 figures, which religious community had the highest sex ratio in India?
accepted.x: Christians had the highest sex ratio among the listed religious communities in 2011, at 1,023 females per 1,000 males. The national average was 943.
accepted.tq: Compare the community values rather than relying on the national average.
accepted.sec: Religion-wise sex ratio and literacy differentials

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the sex-ratio order from highest to lowest among the listed religious communities in 2011?
o: Jains, Christians, Buddhists, Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs
Christians, Buddhists, Jains, Muslims, Hindus, Sikhs
Christians, Jains, Buddhists, Muslims, Hindus, Sikhs
Buddhists, Christians, Muslims, Jains, Hindus, Sikhs
accepted.x: The order was Christians (1,023), Buddhists (965), Jains (954), Muslims (951), Hindus (939) and Sikhs (903). Sikhs had the lowest sex ratio among these communities.
accepted.tq: Arrange the numerical values from highest to lowest and check adjacent comparisons.
accepted.sec: Religion-wise sex ratio and literacy differentials

accepted.s: What was the national average sex ratio in India in 2011 as given in the religious comparison?
accepted.x: The national average sex ratio in 2011 was 943. The figures for individual communities ranged from 903 among Sikhs to 1,023 among Christians.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the national benchmark from the community-specific figures.
accepted.sec: Religion-wise sex ratio and literacy differentials

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding religion-wise literacy in 2011:
1. Jains had the highest literacy rate, at about 95 per cent for the population aged seven years and above.
2. Muslims had the lowest literacy rate among the listed communities.
3. The literacy order placed Christians, Buddhists, Sikhs and Hindus between Jains and Muslims.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The literacy order was Jains, Christians, Buddhists, Sikhs, Hindus and Muslims, with Jains at about 95 per cent and Muslims at the lowest position.
accepted.tq: Use the complete ranking to verify both the extremes and the intervening order.
accepted.sec: Religion-wise sex ratio and literacy differentials

accepted.s: The relatively high literacy and slow growth associated with Jains is linked in the comparison to their being predominantly:
accepted.x: Jains are described as mostly urban and commercial. This profile is associated with their top literacy and slowest growth.
accepted.tq: Connect the social-economic profile with the demographic indicators given.
accepted.sec: Religion-wise sex ratio and literacy differentials

accepted.s: According to Census 2011 figures for residual Andhra Pradesh, which of the following is the correct order of religious shares from highest to lowest?
accepted.x: In residual Andhra Pradesh, Hindus accounted for about 90.9 per cent, Muslims about 7.3 per cent and Christians about 1.4 per cent.
accepted.tq: Compare the percentage shares and identify the descending order.
accepted.sec: Religious composition of AP - shares and minority districts  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The approximate share of Muslims in the population of residual Andhra Pradesh according to Census 2011 was:
accepted.x: Muslims constituted about 7.3 per cent of the population of residual Andhra Pradesh according to Census 2011. The corresponding shares mentioned for Hindus and Christians were about 90.9 per cent and 1.4 per cent.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between close-looking percentages and the overall minority figure.
accepted.sec: Religious composition of AP - shares and minority districts  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Christian population of Andhra Pradesh was estimated at approximately how many persons in APSES 2024–25?
accepted.x: The Christian population of Andhra Pradesh was stated as approximately 6.82 lakh in APSES 2024–25. It is concentrated in coastal districts and tribal agency areas.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact population figure and distinguish it from percentage shares.
accepted.sec: Religious composition of AP - shares and minority districts  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Christian population in Andhra Pradesh is concentrated mainly in:
o: The coastal districts and tribal agency areas
Only the metropolitan region of Visakhapatnam
accepted.x: The Christian population of Andhra Pradesh is concentrated in the coastal districts and tribal agency areas. It is not confined to Rayalaseema or a single metropolitan region.
accepted.tq: Use the location clue and reject options that impose an unsupported exclusive concentration.
accepted.sec: Religious composition of AP - shares and minority districts  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the minority population of Andhra Pradesh?
1. It is mostly urban.
2. It contains a large Below-Poverty-Line segment.
3. It has a low share in economic support schemes.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the minority population of Andhra Pradesh in APSES 2024–25: it is mostly urban, has a large Below-Poverty-Line segment and has a low share in economic support schemes.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of linked social indicators without reversing their direction.
accepted.sec: Religious composition of AP - shares and minority districts  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the highest Muslim population shares are associated with which group of districts?
accepted.x: The highest Muslim shares in Andhra Pradesh are associated with the Rayalaseema districts of Kurnool, YSR Kadapa and Anantapur.
accepted.tq: Match the religious concentration with the correct regional district group.
accepted.sec: Religious composition of AP - shares and minority districts  [GROUP-II]
